name: Jim Justice

issue_poll.name: Emerson College West Virginia poll, March 2024 (most important issue facing WV) + MetroNews West Virginia Poll, Aug 21–27, 2024 (most important national problem); Gallup national, Sept 16–28, 2024
issue_poll.note: Ranks 1–7 come from the two WV polls: Emerson's full list, with immigration and crime moved up per MetroNews (https://wvchamber.com/west-virginia-poll-economy-is-most-important-national-factor-and-respondents-say-its-off-course/). 'Threats to democracy' left out as untestable. Ranks 8–10 filled from Gallup national 'extremely important' shares (https://news.gallup.com/poll/651719/economy-important-issue-2024-presidential-vote.aspx). No full-ranking WV poll near Election Day was found.

issues.position: Clear crypto regulatory framework; oppose a central bank digital currency
issues.note: His campaign pledge to cut spending and the debt was a direction only, so it is not scored.

Protect coverage for people with pre-existing conditions
issues.note: No floor vote directly tested pre-existing condition protections this term.

Leave abortion to states; support federal late-term limits
issues.note: No floor vote on a late-term limit; he voted Yea on Born-Alive cloture (S.6, roll call 11), which is a different policy.

caveats: Issue ranking combines two 2024 WV polls with Gallup national data. No single WV poll near Election Day ranked all issues.
Positions come from his campaign issue pages (jimjusticewv.com), which were read through BallotReady and Marathon Strategies summaries because the site itself could not be reached.
HALT Fentanyl Act Yea is inferred: he cosponsored the bill and praised its 84-16 passage, but no source seen listed his individual vote.
The judicial item is scored on a confirmation vote, not a bill, so the 'bill' field reads 'Nomination'.
